items.prompt: A solid system-design hour sequence starts with?
choices: Clarify requirements and constraints before sketching boxes
items.whyRight: Scope and force ranking prevent ornamental architecture.
whyWrong: Sharding is a late scaling move.

items.prompt: Why reserve minutes at the end to name the bottleneck?
choices: Interviewers grade whether you know what breaks first under load
Bottlenecks only appear in code reviews
items.whyRight: Calling the first fracture shows judgment.

choices: Deepen the riskiest cut; keep other boxes shallow on purpose
items.whyRight: Time-box forces prioritization of the hard edge.
whyWrong: APIs matter but are not the only cut.

choices: Functional behavior vs non-functional bounds (QPS, latency, durability)
items.whyRight: Behavior vs bounds drives different design moves.
whyWrong: UI polish is rarely the system cut.
Vendor is an implementation detail later.

items.prompt: Red flag in a design narrative?
choices: Naming five new mechanisms before one end-to-end path works
items.whyRight: Novelty without a working path is theater.
whyWrong: Rough orders of magnitude are expected.

items.prompt: When the prompt is huge, you should?
choices: Negotiate a thinner MVP that still exercises the core force
Implement every optional feature in the diagram
items.whyRight: A crisp MVP shows product sense and saves depth for the hard part.
